title: 421. Ancient Carthage: Lords of the Sea (Part 1)

sentences.en: Before undertaking anything, it was well to make trial of the arms of the god.
sentences.zh: 在着手做任何事之前，最好先试一试神像的武器。

sentences.en: Slender chainlets stretched from his fingers up to his shoulders and fell behind, where men, by
sentences.zh: 细小的链条从他的手指一直延伸到肩膀，垂在身后，人们通过

sentences.en: pulling them, made the two hands rise to a level with the elbows and come close together against the belly.
sentences.zh: 拉动这些链条，使那两只手抬到与肘部齐平的高度，并向腹部靠拢。

sentences.en: They were moved several times in succession with little abrupt jerks.
sentences.zh: 它们被连续几次猛地拉动。

sentences.en: Then the instruments were still.
sentences.zh: 随后，这些器械静止不动了。

sentences.en: The fire roared.
sentences.zh: 火焰咆哮着。

sentences.en: People flung into the flames pearls, gold vases, cups, torches, all their wealth.
sentences.zh: 人们将珍珠、金瓶、杯子、火把，以及他们所有的财富都抛入火中。

sentences.en: The offerings became constantly more numerous and more splendid.
sentences.zh: 祭品变得越来越丰富，越来越壮观。

sentences.en: At last, a man who tottered, a man pale and hideous with terror, thrust forward a child.
sentences.zh: 最后，一个步履蹒跚、脸色苍白、因恐惧而显得狰狞的男人，推着一个孩子走了上来。

sentences.en: Then a little black mass was seen between the hands of the colossus and sank into the dark opening.
sentences.zh: 接着，人们看到巨像的手中出现了一团黑色的小东西，随后沉入了黑暗的开口中。

sentences.en: The priests bent over the edge of the great flagstone, and a new song burst forth, celebrating the joys of death and of new birth into eternity.
sentences.zh: 祭司们俯身在大石板的边缘，一首新的赞歌响起，歌颂着死亡的喜悦和通往永恒的新生。

sentences.en: The children ascended slowly, and as the smoke formed lofty eddies as it escaped, they seemed, at a distance, to disappear in a cloud.
sentences.zh: 孩子们缓缓上升，随着烟雾在逃逸时形成高高的漩涡，从远处看，他们仿佛消失在云雾中。

sentences.en: The brazen arms were working quickly now.
sentences.zh: 那双青铜手臂现在动作很快。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the appetite of the god was not appeased.
sentences.zh: 然而，神灵的胃口并没有得到满足。

sentences.en: He ever wished for more.
sentences.zh: 他总是想要更多。

sentences.en: In order to furnish him with a larger supply, the victims were piled up on his hands with a big chain above them which kept them in their place.
sentences.zh: 为了给他提供更多的祭品，受害者被堆叠在神像的手上，上面压着一条大铁链，将他们固定在原位。

sentences.en: It was impossible to distinguish them in the giddy motion of the horrible arMs. This lasted for a long, indefinite time, until the evening.
sentences.zh: 在恐怖手臂那令人眩晕的动作中，根本无法分辨出他们。这种情况持续了很长、无法确定的时间，直到傍晚。

sentences.en: Then the partitions inside assumed a darker glow, and burning flesh could be seen.
sentences.zh: 那时，内部的隔板呈现出更深沉的红光，可以看到燃烧的血肉。

sentences.en: Some even believed that they could descry hair, limbs, and whole bodies.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至认为他们能辨认出头发、四肢和完整的躯体。

sentences.en: So, Tom, that is by Gustave Flaubert, the author of Madame Bovary.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，那是古斯塔夫·福楼拜的作品，也就是《包法利夫人》的作者。

sentences.en: It's a very different book.
sentences.zh: 那是一本非常不同的书。

sentences.en: It's his book Salonbo, which was published in 1862.
sentences.zh: 那是他1862年出版的书《萨朗波》。

sentences.en: Very much not set in provincial France.
sentences.zh: 故事背景完全不在法国外省。

sentences.en: No, not the story of a young woman who's been reading too much in their French romantic periodicals.
sentences.zh: 不，那不是一个读了太多法国浪漫主义期刊的年轻女人的故事。

sentences.en: This is very different.
sentences.zh: 这非常不同。

sentences.en: This is set in Carthage.
sentences.zh: 故事发生在迦太基。

sentences.en: And I remember reading this when I was at university and being stunned that it was so different from Madame Bovary,
sentences.zh: 我记得我在大学时读过这本书，当时非常震惊，因为它和《包法利夫人》截然不同，

sentences.en: because what Salonbo does is it plunges you into this incredibly violent, lurid, orientalist fantasy of ancient Carthage, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为《萨朗波》让你沉浸在古迦太基那种极其暴力、耸人听闻、东方主义色彩浓厚的幻想中，不是吗？

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And this is set against a very particular episode.
sentences.zh: 而且故事背景设定在一个非常特殊的时期。

sentences.en: And it's not one of the most famous episodes in Carthaginian history.
sentences.zh: 它并不是迦太基历史上最著名的事件之一。

sentences.en: It directly follows on from the first great war that the Carthaginians fought against the Romans, the first Punic war, as it's called.
sentences.zh: 它紧接着迦太基人与罗马人之间进行的第一场大战，也就是所谓的第一次布匿战争。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the Carthaginians have been defeated, and they've had to pay reparations to the Romans.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人战败了，不得不向罗马人支付赔款。

sentences.en: And as a result, they can't pay their mercenaries, which they've been employing to conduct the war.
sentences.zh: 结果，他们无法支付雇佣军的薪水，而这些雇佣军正是他们用来进行战争的。

sentences.en: And so the mercenaries have turned on Carthage and put it under siege.
sentences.zh: 于是，雇佣军反戈一击，将迦太基围困起来。

sentences.en: And it looks like the city may be about to be captured.
sentences.zh: 看起来这座城市即将被攻陷。

sentences.en: And the great Carthaginian general, the commander who had remained undefeated in the war against the Romans, Hamilcar Barca,
sentences.zh: 而那位伟大的迦太基将军，那位在对罗马战争中保持不败的指挥官——汉尼拔·巴卡，

sentences.en: has been summoned to join the rest of the Carthaginian elite to pay the ultimate sacrifice, which is to give their firstborn to the great god Moloch.
sentences.zh: 已被召回，与迦太基的其他精英一起做出终极牺牲，即将他们的长子献给伟大的神摩洛克。

sentences.en: So it is the god Moloch whose hands have been moving up and down with the great golden chain.
sentences.zh: 所以，正是摩洛克神的手臂在随着那条巨大的金链上下移动。

sentences.en: It's very Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这非常有《印第安纳·琼斯与魔宫传奇》的感觉，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's the sacrifice scene in the Temple of Doom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是《魔宫传奇》里的祭祀场景。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实是。

sentences.en: And that, of course, I guess, would be playing on exactly this scene.
sentences.zh: 我想，那当然是在影射这一幕。

sentences.en: And Hamilcar does not want to sacrifice his son called Hannibal.
sentences.zh: 汉尼拔不想牺牲他的儿子，也叫汉尼拔。

sentences.en: And so he has got a slave boy instead and swapped them.
sentences.zh: 所以他找了一个奴隶男孩代替，把他们调换了。

sentences.en: And of course, this means that Hamilcar's son Hannibal survives.
sentences.zh: 当然，这意味着汉尼拔的儿子汉尼拔活了下来。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Hannibal will go on to grow up and become the most famous of all Carthaginians.
sentences.zh: 而汉尼拔长大后，成为了所有迦太基人中最著名的一位。

sentences.en: The man who leads elephants over the Alps brings Rome almost to its knees.
sentences.zh: 那个带领大象翻越阿尔卑斯山，几乎让罗马屈膝的人。

sentences.en: And the story of Hannibal's war against the
sentences.zh: 而汉尼拔对阵

sentences.en: Romans is probably the most famous war, actually, in the whole of ancient history.
sentences.zh: 罗马人的战争，实际上可能是整个古代史上最著名的战争。

sentences.en: But we are not going to be focusing on Hannibal's war, but on the early history of Carthage in this series.
sentences.zh: 但我们这一系列节目不会专注于汉尼拔的战争，而是关注迦太基的早期历史。

sentences.en: So, Tom, that war that you described with the mercenaries, that's 238 BC.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，你描述的那场与雇佣军的战争，发生在公元前238年。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we'll be getting sort of towards that, but just on the Orientalism and whatnot of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将会谈到那个时期，但先聊聊迦太基的东方主义之类的东西。

sentences.en: So even people who know nothing about ancient history will have heard the name, won't they?
sentences.zh: 所以即使是对古代历史一无所知的人，也听说过这个名字，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, there are Carthages in the United States, for example, named after the city.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美国就有以这座城市命名的迦太基。

sentences.en: And I guess the reputation of Carthage, even among people who don't know much about it, is that, you know, Rome is disciplined, formidable, clean shaven, all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 我想迦太基的声誉，即使在不太了解它的人中，也是这样的：你知道，罗马是纪律严明、强大、剃须干净的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And Carthage is exotic, cruel, luxurious, decadent.
sentences.zh: 而迦太基则是异国情调、残忍、奢华、颓废的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: As you said, unbelievably cruel.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，难以置信的残忍。

sentences.en: Child sacrifice is obviously a massive element of that.
sentences.zh: 活人祭祀显然是其中一个巨大的因素。

sentences.en: These incredibly weird and terrifying gods, but also rich and entrepreneurial.
sentences.zh: 这些极其怪异和可怕的神灵，但同时也富有且具有商业头脑。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the French, after the French Revolution, when they thought that they were the Romans, they used to say that the British were the Carthaginians, because all we cared about was
sentences.zh: 所以法国大革命后的法国人，当他们认为自己是罗马人时，他们常说英国人是迦太基人，因为我们关心的只是

sentences.en: making money.
sentences.zh: 赚钱。

sentences.en: But also because Carthage was a great maritime power.
sentences.zh: 但也因为迦太基是一个伟大的海上强国。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And of course, Rome is a great land power.
sentences.zh: 当然，罗马是一个伟大的陆地强国。

sentences.en: And so their war was often characterized as, you know, the war between the elephant and the whale.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的战争常被描述为，你知道，大象与鲸鱼之间的战争。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 就是那种感觉。

sentences.en: And so the French were very keen to brand the British as Carthaginian, both because they were seen as being treacherous, mercantilist, but also of course,
sentences.zh: 所以法国人非常热衷于给英国人贴上迦太基人的标签，既因为他们被视为背信弃义、重商主义，也当然是因为

sentences.en: because ultimately Carthage loses and gets obliterated, but is commemorated by the Romans as her greatest enemy.
sentences.zh: 最终迦太基战败并被彻底摧毁，但被罗马人铭记为他们最强大的敌人。

sentences.en: And Hannibal is, you know, seen as the most forbiddable opponent that the
sentences.zh: 而汉尼拔，你知道，被视为

sentences.en: Romans ever fought.
sentences.zh: 罗马人所对抗过的最强大的对手。

sentences.en: And so that's a crucial part of why the memory of Carthage endures.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是迦太基的记忆能够长存的关键原因。

sentences.en: And so we'll be covering the first of those great wars in the fourth of our episodes.
sentences.zh: 我们将在第四集节目中讲述这些伟大战争中的第一场。

sentences.en: But before that, we want to look at what the origins are of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，我们想看看迦太基的起源是什么。

sentences.en: What's the characteristics of our civilization?
sentences.zh: 我们文明的特征是什么？

sentences.en: Did they really sacrifice their children or is that just kind of Roman propaganda?
sentences.zh: 他们真的牺牲了自己的孩子，还是那只是罗马的宣传？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: To try and kind of bring back to life this extraordinary civilization, which has been, I think, kind of blackened so repeatedly over the course of history.
sentences.zh: 试图让这个非凡的文明重现生机，我认为它在历史上被反复抹黑。

sentences.en: And Tom, just for people who don't know, so Carthage is effectively on the site of present day
sentences.zh: 汤姆，对于那些不知道的人，迦太基实际上位于现今的

sentences.en: Tunis, the capital of Tunisia in North Africa.
sentences.zh: 突尼斯，即北非突尼斯的首都。

sentences.en: And almost all the traces, I mean, if you've ever been to Tunis, I've been to Tunis.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有的痕迹，我的意思是，如果你去过突尼斯，我去过突尼斯。

sentences.en: I actually thought it was a bit disappointing because almost every single trace of ancient Carthage, apart from your little bit of stone, has been erased.
sentences.zh: 我其实觉得有点失望，因为除了你那一点点石头，古迦太基的几乎每一丝痕迹都被抹去了。

sentences.en: Well, we might come to that in a minute, but this isn't the first episode that we've done on Carthage.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们一会儿可能会谈到这一点，但这并不是我们做的第一期关于迦太基的节目。

sentences.en: So in the World Cup, we did one.
sentences.zh: 在世界杯期间，我们做过一期。

sentences.en: Tunisia were playing in the World Cup.
sentences.zh: 突尼斯队参加了世界杯。

sentences.en: And so our episode was on the founding of Carthage, which is a kind of famous legend because it was enshrined by Virgil in the Aeneid.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的节目是关于迦太基的建立，这是一个著名的传说，因为它被维吉尔写进了《埃涅阿斯纪》中。

sentences.en: And it described how Aeneas, who is a prince fleeing Troy, who is fated by the gods to go to Italy and their father, the line of kings that will culminate in the founding of Rome.
sentences.zh: 它描述了埃涅阿斯，一位逃离特洛伊的王子，命中注定要前往意大利，并成为最终建立罗马的国王世系的祖先。

sentences.en: But he stops off in what is now Tunisia.
sentences.zh: 但他中途停在了现在的突尼斯。

sentences.en: And he sees there the founding of a city by a woman from a city called Tyre.
sentences.zh: 他在那里看到一个来自泰尔城的女人建立了一座城市。

sentences.en: And this woman is called Dido, but she's also known as Elissa.
sentences.zh: 这个女人叫狄多，但她也被称为埃丽莎。

sentences.en: And she has come from what is now Lebanon.
sentences.zh: 她来自现在的黎巴嫩。

sentences.en: So in ancient times, it was called Canaan.
sentences.zh: 在古代，那里被称为迦南。

sentences.en: So she is a Tyrian princess.
sentences.zh: 所以她是一位泰尔公主。

sentences.en: And the story goes, and this is a story that doesn't feature in Virgil's account, but was kind of repeatedly told by Greek and Roman historians, that she had been married to her
sentences.zh: 故事是这样的，这在维吉尔的记述中没有出现，但被希腊和罗马历史学家反复讲述，她曾嫁给她的

sentences.en: uncle, a guy called Akurbas.
sentences.zh: 叔叔，一个叫阿库巴斯的人。

sentences.en: And Dido's brother, a man called Pygmalion, was the king of Tyre, was very, very jealous of Akurbas because Akurbas was so rich.
sentences.zh: 狄多的兄弟，一个叫皮格马利翁的人，是泰尔的国王，他非常嫉妒阿库巴斯，因为阿库巴斯太有钱了。

sentences.en: And so he has Akurbas murdered.
sentences.zh: 于是他谋杀了阿库巴斯。

sentences.en: And he then wants to seize Akurbas's wealth.
sentences.zh: 然后他想夺取阿库巴斯的财富。

sentences.en: But before he can do that, Dido makes an offering of it to the gods by putting all the gold into sacks and throwing it into the sea.
sentences.zh: 但在他这样做之前，狄多把所有的金子装进袋子里扔进海里，以此作为对神的祭献。

sentences.en: But in fact, Dominic, the sacks are full of sand, not gold.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，多米尼克，那些袋子里装的是沙子，而不是金子。

sentences.en: What an amazing trick, Tom.
sentences.zh: 多么精彩的诡计啊，汤姆。

sentences.en: And she has taken the gold and she sails off, heads west to found Carthage.
sentences.zh: 她拿走了金子，扬帆起航，向西前往建立迦太基。

sentences.en: And this is clearly a myth.
sentences.zh: 这显然是一个神话。

sentences.en: I mean, it has a myth all over it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它充满了神话色彩。

sentences.en: But what's intriguing is that there are echoes of
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，在古典名字中存在着

sentences.en: authentic Tyrian names in the classical names.
sentences.zh: 真实的泰尔名字的回响。

sentences.en: So Pygmalion, Pumayaton, Elissa, Dido, Elishat, and Akurbas, Zakabal.
sentences.zh: 比如皮格马利翁（Pumayaton），埃丽莎（Dido/Elishat），以及阿库巴斯（Zakabal）。

sentences.en: These names do seem to come from genuinely Tyrian sources.
sentences.zh: 这些名字似乎确实来自真正的泰尔语源。

sentences.en: And the other thing, of course, that thing of throwing gold away, of making it as an offering to the gods.
sentences.zh: 当然还有另一件事，那种把金子扔掉、作为祭品献给神灵的行为。

sentences.en: I mean, that is kind of echoed a little bit in Salambo.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这在《萨朗波》中得到了一点呼应。

sentences.en: Before they start sacrificing the children, they are hurling in their jewels and their necklaces and their gold to the flames.
sentences.zh: 在他们开始牺牲孩子之前，他们正把珠宝、项链和金子扔进火焰中。

sentences.en: So perhaps there's kind of elements there.
sentences.zh: 所以也许那里有一些元素。

sentences.en: And one thing that is absolutely certain is that Carthage really was founded by colonists from Tyre.
sentences.zh: 有一点是绝对肯定的，那就是迦太基确实是由来自泰尔的殖民者建立的。

sentences.en: From Lebanon.
sentences.zh: 来自黎巴嫩。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the city in Lebanon.
sentences.zh: 也就是黎巴嫩的那座城市。

sentences.en: And we know this from a very famous detail that is recorded by
sentences.zh: 我们从希罗多德记录的一个非常著名的细节中得知这一点。

sentences.en: Herodotus.
sentences.zh: 泰尔最终被波斯国王征服了。

sentences.en: So Tyre ends up being conquered by the Persian kings.
sentences.zh: 居鲁士大帝的儿子，所有波斯国王中第一位也是最强大的一位，一个叫冈比西斯的人，他征服了埃及。

sentences.en: And the son of Cyrus the Great, the first and most formidable of all the Persian kings, a guy called Cambyses, he conquers Egypt.
sentences.zh: 然后他想继续向西征服迦太基。

sentences.en: And then he wants to press on westwards and conquer Carthage.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，他需要泰尔舰队的协助，因为泰尔是一座伟大的水手之城。

sentences.en: And to do that, he needs the assistance of a Tyrian fleet, because Tyre is a great city of sailors.
sentences.zh: 泰尔人拒绝参与，理由是迦太基人是他们的孩子，而且迦太基人仍然会回到泰尔进行祭献。

sentences.en: And the Tyrians refuse to participate on the basis that the Carthaginians are their children and that the Carthaginians still come to Tyre to make offerings.
sentences.zh: 事实上，多米尼克，你还记得亚历山大大帝后来围攻并占领了泰尔。

sentences.en: So Carolina Lopez-Riez argues that they did call themselves Canaanites, which has kind of been the traditional view.
sentences.zh: 所以卡罗琳娜·洛佩兹-里兹认为他们确实称自己为迦南人，这在某种程度上是传统的观点。

sentences.en: And I mean, this is how the biblical writers frame them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是《圣经》作者对他们的描述方式。

sentences.en: So they do frame the people of Tyre as worshipers of Canaanite gods.
sentences.zh: 他们确实将推罗人描述为迦南神灵的崇拜者。

sentences.en: So in the first book of Chronicles, a guy called Canaan is the father of Sidon.
sentences.zh: 所以在《历代志》第一卷中，一个叫迦南的人是西顿的父亲。

sentences.en: So, you know, Canaan gives his name to the land and he's the father of Sidon, who then goes on to found the city.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，迦南给了这片土地他的名字，他是西顿的父亲，西顿后来建立了这座城市。

sentences.en: So I think that it's not just the Greeks who are seeing the people of Tyre and Sidon as distinctive.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为不仅仅是希腊人将推罗和西顿的人视为独特的。

sentences.en: I think the Israelites are doing that as well, because Sidon and Tyre are both seen as providing good things, cedar and craftsmen and things like that, and of dangerous things.
sentences.zh: 我认为以色列人也是这样做的，因为西顿和推罗都被视为既提供好东西——雪松、工匠之类——也提供危险的东西。

sentences.en: So in one of the biblical accounts of the life of Jezebel, she's described as being a princess of Sidon, not of Tyre.
sentences.zh: 所以在《圣经》关于耶洗别生平的记载中，她被描述为西顿的公主，而不是推罗的。

sentences.en: So you have there a sense that she's interchangeable.
sentences.zh: 所以你从中感觉到她是可互换的。

sentences.en: It's like Wolverhampton and Birmingham, Tom.
sentences.zh: 就像伍尔弗汉普顿和伯明翰一样，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: People from outside foolishly can't tell the enormous difference between those two places.
sentences.zh: 外地人愚蠢地看不出这两个地方之间的巨大差异。

sentences.en: Actually, I think the obvious comparison is with the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我认为明显的比较对象是希腊人。

sentences.en: You know, there aren't actually that many passages where Greeks talk about there being a Hellenic culture and we don't really have any, let's call it Phoenician literature.
sentences.zh: 你知道，实际上并没有多少段落提到希腊人谈论存在一种希腊文化，而且我们真的没有任何——我们称之为腓尼基文学的东西。

sentences.en: So even Josephine Quinn, although she denies the existence of Phoenicians, she's always using Phoenicians in inverted commas.
sentences.zh: 所以即使是约瑟芬·奎因，尽管她否认腓尼基人的存在，她也总是把“腓尼基人”放在引号里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I think even, you know, that is betraying the fact that there is a kind of common culture there.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为即使是这一点，也暴露了那里存在一种共同文化的事实。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So whether you want to call them Phoenicians or Phoenicians in inverted commas, I think there probably is.
sentences.zh: 所以无论你想称呼他们为腓尼基人，还是带引号的“腓尼基人”，我认为可能确实存在。

sentences.en: So I think that the sense that you get in both the Bible and in Greek accounts, that the Phoenicians are formidable sailors and that they are spectacularly wealthy,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在《圣经》和希腊记载中，腓尼基人是强大的水手且极其富有，这种感觉，

sentences.en: I think that these probably would have been recognized by the Phoenicians themselves as giving them a kind of common identity.
sentences.zh: 我认为腓尼基人自己可能也会承认这赋予了他们一种共同的身份。

sentences.en: But it is sharpened in the Greek case because the Greeks, in a sense, you know, they are direct rivals, what we were saying before the break,
sentences.zh: 但在希腊人的情况下，这种认同感被强化了，因为希腊人在某种意义上，你知道，他们是直接的竞争对手，就像我们在休息前说的那样，

sentences.en: that the Greeks recognize themselves in the Phoenicians.
sentences.zh: 希腊人在腓尼基人身上看到了自己的影子。

sentences.en: And that's why the rivalry between them I think is so kind of intense because the Greeks know that they are following in the Phoenician way.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为他们之间的竞争如此激烈，因为希腊人知道他们是在追随腓尼基人的道路。

sentences.en: It's the Phoenicians have given them the alphabet, which has enabled writing to flourish, which in turn facilitates trade.
sentences.zh: 是腓尼基人给了他们字母表，这使得书写得以繁荣，进而促进了贸易。

sentences.en: But when the Greeks start spreading westwards to set up their own trade network, they find that the Phoenicians have got there before them,
sentences.zh: 但是当希腊人开始向西扩张以建立自己的贸易网络时，他们发现腓尼基人已经先他们一步到达了那里，

sentences.en: that the Phoenicians have occupied all the best spots because it's the Phoenicians who basically
sentences.zh: 腓尼基人占据了所有最好的位置，因为基本上是腓尼基人

sentences.en: establish the Mediterranean as a kind of common sea that enable the silver and the iron ore of Spain
sentences.zh: 将地中海建立成了一种共同的海域，使得西班牙和意大利的白银和铁矿石

sentences.en: and Italy to be brought to the Near East and for Near Eastern fashions to be taken to Italy and to
sentences.zh: 能够被运往近东，而近东的时尚能够被带到意大利、撒丁岛

sentences.en: Sardinia and Spain.
sentences.zh: 和西班牙。

sentences.en: And when are we talking about here, Tom?
sentences.zh: 我们在这里谈论的是什么时候，汤姆？

sentences.en: I mean, 500 BC, further back, 1000 BC?
sentences.zh: 我是说，公元前500年，更早，公元前1000年？

sentences.en: Farther back, say 900, 800, 700.
sentences.zh: 更早，比如公元前900年、800年、700年。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So well before the golden age of Greece.
sentences.zh: 所以远在希腊黄金时代之前。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And the Phoenicians have been able to do this because as they've been doing since the third century millennium, they are at the cutting edge of maritime innovation.
sentences.zh: 腓尼基人之所以能做到这一点，是因为正如他们从公元前三千年就开始做的那样，他们处于海上创新的最前沿。

sentences.en: So they are building faster ships.
sentences.zh: 所以他们建造了更快的船只。

sentences.en: They are coating the hulls with bitumen.
sentences.zh: 他们用沥青涂抹船体。

sentences.en: So they're the first to do that, to ensure that the water doesn't seep through.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是第一个这样做的人，以确保水不会渗进来。

sentences.en: And their ships are so streamlined that basically they can travel up to 30 miles a day.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的船只非常流线型，基本上每天可以航行多达30英里。

sentences.en: You know, that's incredibly quick.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这非常快。

sentences.en: And also they can travel at night because they are the people who have developed the use of the pole star.
sentences.zh: 而且他们也可以在夜间航行，因为他们是开发了北极星用法的人。

sentences.en: So they can use that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可以使用那个。

sentences.en: And the Greeks themselves call the pole star, the Phoenicae.
sentences.zh: 希腊人自己称北极星为“腓尼基星”。

sentences.en: So they are branding the pole star as Phoenician.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把北极星标记为腓尼基的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's this that has enabled the Phoenicians to plant colonies right the way across Southern Africa, including Carthage, supposedly in 814 BC.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点使腓尼基人能够在整个南非建立殖民地，包括据称在公元前814年建立的迦太基。

sentences.en: But going onwards, Sardinia, Sicily, Southern Spain, and out into the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 此后，还有撒丁岛、西西里岛、西班牙南部，并进入大西洋。

sentences.en: So we mentioned Gardez.
sentences.zh: 所以我们提到了加的斯。

sentences.en: And there are some stories, aren't there, Tom?
sentences.zh: 而且有一些故事，不是吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: There are sort of exaggerated myths and stuff that they went as far as Cornwall or indeed North America, which I imagine people think now is obviously total tosh.
sentences.zh: 有一些夸张的神话之类的，说他们走到了康沃尔甚至北美，我想人们现在认为这显然是彻头彻尾的胡说八道。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So the Phoenicians are always looking for raw materials.
sentences.zh: 所以腓尼基人一直在寻找原材料。

sentences.en: They're looking for gold, for silver, for copper, for iron, and of course, for tin.
sentences.zh: 他们在寻找黄金、白银、铜、铁，当然还有锡。

sentences.en: To get this, they are going beyond the pillars of Hercules.
sentences.zh: 为了得到这些，他们越过了赫拉克勒斯之柱。

sentences.en: They are definitely planting colonies in the Atlantic, Iberia, and Atlantic, North Africa.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对在大西洋、伊比利亚和大西洋北非建立了殖民地。

sentences.en: What's that, Portugal or what's now Morocco?
sentences.zh: 那是哪里，葡萄牙还是现在的摩洛哥？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Basically, yeah.
sentences.zh: 基本上是这样。

sentences.en: Whether they go as far as Cornwall, I mean, this is a tradition that's obviously very popular with the
sentences.zh: 他们是否真的去过康沃尔，我的意思是，这显然是一个在当地非常流行的传统，

sentences.en: Cornish.
sentences.zh: 康沃尔人。

sentences.en: There's no archaeological evidence for it.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有考古学证据支持。

sentences.en: There's no explicit written evidence for it.
sentences.zh: 也没有明确的文字记载。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But there is, I mean, this kind of classic ancient history, there is a poem that is written in late antiquity that is drawing on a fifth-century poem.
sentences.zh: 但确实有，我是说，这是一种经典的古代历史，有一首写于古典时代晚期的诗，它借鉴了一首五世纪的诗作。

sentences.en: What, a thousand years later?
sentences.zh: 什么，一千年以后？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, sorry, Tom, I'd need a bit more than that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，抱歉，汤姆，我需要比这更有力的证据。

sentences.en: I know you do.
sentences.zh: 我知道你需要。

sentences.en: And this mentions a guy called
sentences.zh: 这首诗提到了一个叫

sentences.en: Himilco, who sails out into the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 希米尔科的人，他航行到了大西洋。

sentences.en: And he brings tin back from a place called the Cassiterides, which might be Cornwall, but equally, you know, it could be Northern Iberia or whatever.
sentences.zh: 他从一个叫卡西特拉德斯的地方带回了锡，那可能是康沃尔，但同样地，你知道，也可能是伊比利亚北部或其他什么地方。

sentences.en: I mean, it could be.
sentences.zh: 我是说，完全有可能。

sentences.en: It could be Porto.
sentences.zh: 可能是波尔图。

sentences.en: But also, we're told in this poem that Himilco had sailed out into the Atlantic Ocean and had found there that the sea was covered with thick seaweed.
sentences.zh: 但我们也从这首诗中得知，希米尔科曾航行到大西洋，发现那里的海面覆盖着厚厚的海藻。

sentences.en: And so it has been posited that perhaps this was the Sargasso Sea.
sentences.zh: 因此有人推测，这或许就是马尾藻海。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Of course, people have wanted to believe that they might have sailed all the way to America.
sentences.zh: 当然，人们一直希望相信他们可能一路航行到了美洲。

sentences.en: And there have been kind of various faked, you know, lumps of stone with Phoenician writing inscribed in it.
sentences.zh: 而且还有各种伪造的，你知道，刻有腓尼基文字的石块。

sentences.en: But these are all fakes.
sentences.zh: 但这些全是伪造的。

sentences.en: There's no hard evidence at all.
sentences.zh: 根本没有任何确凿的证据。

sentences.en: Tom, you've lost all our listeners in the Lebanese-American community with this skepticism.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你这种怀疑态度已经让所有黎巴嫩裔美国听众都离你而去了。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 是啊，好吧，我很抱歉。

sentences.en: But there is also evidence from a Greek text called the Periplus, so the sailing round, that a guy called Hanno might have sailed very, very far south,
sentences.zh: 但还有来自一部名为《航海记》的希腊文本的证据，也就是环航记录，提到一个叫汉诺的人可能航行到了非常、非常遥远的南方，

sentences.en: down the coast of Africa, sourcing kind of ivory, sourcing those apes, perhaps, that were referenced in the Bible.
sentences.zh: 沿着非洲海岸，搜寻象牙，搜寻那些或许在《圣经》中被提及的猿猴。

sentences.en: And we know that he sees creatures that almost certainly were chimpanzees.
sentences.zh: 而且我们知道，他看到的生物几乎可以肯定是黑猩猩。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there's definitely a sense, I think, that, you know, the Phoenicians are really, really formidable sailors.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，人们确实有一种感觉，你知道，腓尼基人是非常、非常强大的航海家。

sentences.en: And Tom, let's get to Carthage.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们来谈谈迦太基吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: So they're going around, establishing these colonies, probably not in Cornwall, but at least on the shores of the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 所以他们四处航行，建立殖民地，可能不是在康沃尔，但至少是在地中海沿岸。

sentences.en: And obviously, the most famous, the one that we began with, is the great city of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 显然，最著名的一个，也就是我们开头提到的，就是伟大的迦太基城。

sentences.en: So, I mean, the traditional date for that is 814 BC.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，传统的建城日期是公元前814年。

sentences.en: Is that plausible?
sentences.zh: 这可信吗？

sentences.en: I think it's highly plausible.
sentences.zh: 我认为非常可信。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a lot more plausible than the date that Virgil gives it, which is, of course, around the time of the Trojan War.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这比维吉尔给出的日期要可信得多，当然，维吉尔说的是特洛伊战争时期。

sentences.en: That is not when Carthage is founded.
sentences.zh: 那并不是迦太基建立的时间。

sentences.en: But yes, so probably mid to late 9th century BC, around when the traditional date is.
sentences.zh: 但没错，所以很可能是在公元前九世纪中后期，也就是传统日期左右。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems entirely plausible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来完全可信。

sentences.en: And it's one of a number of colonies that are being planted by the Tyrians at this time.
sentences.zh: 它是当时泰尔人建立的众多殖民地之一。

sentences.en: So there's also Utica, which is where Cato, the younger in due course, will commit suicide.
sentences.zh: 此外还有乌提卡，小加图后来就是在那里自杀的。

sentences.en: But that was originally called the old city.
sentences.zh: 但那个地方最初被称为“旧城”。

sentences.en: And Carthage is the new city.
sentences.zh: 而迦太基是“新城”。

sentences.en: That's what it means.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的意思。

sentences.en: So, you know, you have a sense there that Carthage is perhaps not even the oldest colony being planted by the Tyrians.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你会感觉到迦太基甚至可能不是泰尔人建立的最古老的殖民地。

sentences.en: But as I say, by around 700 BC, you have Phoenician cities,
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，到公元前700年左右，你已经有了腓尼基城市，

sentences.en: Phoenician trading posts everywhere from the Atlantic to the Levant.
sentences.zh: 从大西洋到黎凡特，到处都是腓尼基贸易站。

sentences.en: And as I said, nothing like it has been seen in the Mediterranean before.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，在地中海历史上此前从未见过这样的景象。

sentences.en: So the Phoenicians, or Phoenicians in inverted commas, I mean, these are really, really significant players in the development of trade and
sentences.zh: 所以腓尼基人，或者说加了引号的“腓尼基人”，我的意思是，他们在贸易的发展中，

sentences.en: in the development of the Mediterranean, the sense of the Mediterranean as a kind of single sea.
sentences.zh: 以及在地中海的发展中，在将地中海视为一个统一海域的意识形成中，确实是非常、非常重要的角色。

sentences.en: And evidence for the success of the Phoenicians in kind of cornering Mediterranean trade,
sentences.zh: 我认为腓尼基人在垄断地中海贸易方面取得成功的证据，

sentences.en: I think is found in their very name.
sentences.zh: 就在他们的名字里。

sentences.en: So this word phoenix, which the Greeks say comes from, you know, this Lebanese king called phoenix.
sentences.zh: 这个词“phoenix”，希腊人说它来自，你知道，一位叫菲尼克斯的黎巴嫩国王。

sentences.en: Actually, it means perhaps palm tree.
sentences.zh: 实际上，它可能意味着棕榈树。

sentences.en: So in the late fifth century, Carthage starts minting coins with a palm tree on it as a way of kind of advertising herself to the Greek world that she has a Phoenician identity.
sentences.zh: 所以在五世纪末，迦太基开始铸造印有棕榈树的硬币，以此向希腊世界宣传自己拥有腓尼基身份。

sentences.en: But it's likelier that it comes from the Greek word for kind of reddish purple.
sentences.zh: 但更有可能的是，它源自希腊语中表示某种红紫色的词。

sentences.en: And the color of purple, let's call it purple, comes from probably the most famous of all the Phoenician luxury products,
sentences.zh: 而这种紫色，我们姑且称之为紫色，来自所有腓尼基奢侈品中最著名的一种，

sentences.en: which is a dye, which is made from mucus secreted by a distinctive kind of predatory mollusk called the murex.
sentences.zh: 那就是染料，它是由一种被称为骨螺的独特掠食性软体动物分泌的粘液制成的。

sentences.en: And these mollusks are found in the Eastern Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 这些软体动物分布在地中海东部。

sentences.en: They're also found on the Atlantic coast of Morocco.
sentences.zh: 在摩洛哥的大西洋沿岸也能找到它们。

sentences.en: And the mucus is secreted, I gather specifically, from the hypobranchial glands.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，这种粘液是专门从鳃下腺分泌出来的。

sentences.en: And you can either do it by kind of tickling the mollusks and secreting the mucus that way, or you can just crush their skulls and pull the kind of the flesh out.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过“逗弄”这些软体动物来让它们分泌粘液，或者直接压碎它们的头骨，把肉取出来。

sentences.en: And when you've pulled the flesh out, you leave it to dry in the sun, and then you add salt water, depending on how rich you want the color of the dye to be.
sentences.zh: 取出肉后，放在阳光下晒干，然后加入盐水，这取决于你想要染料的颜色有多浓郁。

sentences.en: Of course, I mean, it absolutely stinks.
sentences.zh: 当然，我的意思是，这绝对臭气熏天。

sentences.en: So this is why the dye factories are always on the edge of towns.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么染料工厂总是建在城镇边缘的原因。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So in Sidon, they found one, a pile of shells that's over 130 meters high.
sentences.zh: 在西顿，他们发现了一个遗址，那里堆积的贝壳超过130米高。

sentences.en: So a lot of mollusks are being killed in the cause of making this dye.
sentences.zh: 所以为了制造这种染料，大量的软体动物被杀死了。

sentences.en: And it's a very specialized process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常专业的过程。

sentences.en: So even to this day, it's not really fully understood.
sentences.zh: 所以直到今天，人们还没有完全弄明白。

sentences.en: And this is the origin of Tyrian purple, which is an expression we still use.
sentences.zh: 这就是“泰尔紫”的起源，这个表达我们至今仍在使用。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
